dedupe_keys.name: legacy 2g 3g networks in mobile resilience southern brazil flood of may 2024

description: This paper investigates how mobile communication networks performed during the extreme flooding that hit Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, in May 2024. Using regulatory data and technical insights from operators, it identifies the leading causes of mobile network disruptions, primarily flooding and prolonged power outages. The results show significant vulnerability of modern 4G and 5G networks during the event and the essential role of legacy 2G and 3G technologies in sustaining basic connectivity under adverse conditions. The authors argue for disaster-aware infrastructure planning that keeps legacy systems in view, diversifies power supply and uses resilient network designs. Producer: Meyer, Granville and Bertholdo, submitted to arXiv on 10 September 2025 as a six-page preprint to appear at IEEE GLOBECOM 2025, before peer review. Coverage: one state of southern Brazil. Access: free PDF and HTML on arXiv. Licence and cost: free; the licence is arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: the paper is a preprint with four figures, the regulatory dataset is not itself offered on the abstract page, and results describe one event. Simulation uses: it supplies observed failure causes and technology-dependence findings to calibrate flood and power-outage scenarios for mobile network resilience models, including decisions on retaining 2G and 3G layers. It is a companion to the 30-day flood telecommunications study of the same event.
